title: Searching for a God Who Hides
overview: Job longs to stand before God and argue his innocence, but he cannot find God anywhere and is left both confident and afraid.

parts.label: Still bitter today (vv. 1-2)
parts.note: Job answers his friend Eliphaz, who has just urged him to make peace with God as if Job were guilty. Job says his pain is still crushing and his complaints do not even match how heavy it is; one word here is hard to read and may mean his friends call his complaint rebellion.

parts.label: If only I could find him (vv. 3-7)
parts.note: Job pictures God seated on a judge's throne and wishes he could go there, lay out his case in order and hear God's reply for himself. He believes a fair hearing would clear him, because God would listen rather than simply overpower him.

parts.label: God is nowhere to be seen (vv. 8-9)
parts.note: Job looks in every direction and finds no sign of God; the Hebrew words for forward, back, left and right also mean east, west, north and south, since people then oriented themselves facing sunrise. He senses God is at work somewhere but cannot catch sight of him.

parts.label: Tested like gold (vv. 10-12)
parts.note: Even so, Job is sure God knows the path he has walked, and that testing will show him pure, like gold that comes out of the fire refined. He insists he has followed God's ways closely and valued God's words more than his daily food.

parts.label: Fear of an unchangeable will (vv. 13-17)
parts.note: Job admits God does whatever he decides, no one can turn him, and more suffering may still be planned, and this terrifies him. The last verse is unclear in Hebrew: it may mean Job refuses to be silenced by the darkness over him, or that he wishes he had died before it came.

disagreement: Christians differ on whether Job's demand to argue his case with God is a model of honest faith or a bold impatience that oversteps, since the book later has God both challenge Job and say Job spoke rightly.
think: If you could lay your hardest experience before someone who had to listen fairly, what would you most want to say, and what would you most want to hear back?
